content.text:
I'm fairly confident only one candidate is present: **mp-1176805 (Li8VO6)**. I simulated three candidates (RbO2, Li8VO6 and FeSbO4) and compared each to the observed pattern by eye.

- **Li8VO6 matches the observed peaks.** The simulated pattern has peaks at about 17.65°, 19.55°, 22.3°, 37.7°, 50.75° and 61.8° two-theta. Their relative heights (about 38, 92, 73, 100, 69 and 41) match the observed strongest peaks closely.
- **The weaker peaks also line up** with the simulation, including those near 30.3°, 34.5°, 38.8°, 47.5°, 53° and 54.5°.
- **I found no peaks that a second phase would be needed to explain.** Some weak high-angle peaks above about 58° could only be matched approximately by eye, so a small amount of a second phase can't be fully ruled out.
- **RbO2 and FeSbO4 don't fit.** Their strongest simulated peaks fall in the 25–45° range, where the observed pattern has no matching strong peaks.

I did not simulate the other six candidates.
